references.text: Balaam lifts his eyes and begins to speak his prophetic word, the same introductory action as here
The expression 'lifts his eyes' is used when someone looks out over a land or people, as when God told Abram to look out over the land
Israel organized according to its tribes, just as Jacob blessed his twelve sons who became the tribes of Israel
Israel's camp was arranged by the tribes, just as Balaam saw them lying there
The Spirit of God comes upon people to give them prophetic ability, just as it came upon the seventy elders
The Spirit of God came upon Saul and he prophesied, using the same expression 'the Spirit of God came upon him'
The Spirit of God came upon Saul's messengers and they prophesied, showing the Spirit's power to give prophetic speech
The Spirit of the Lord came upon Azariah so that he prophesied, a parallel to the Spirit coming upon Balaam
The Spirit of God came upon Zechariah so that he prophesied, following the same pattern of the Spirit's power
The Spirit of the Lord fell upon Ezekiel and gave him a prophetic message
Prophecy never came by human will, but by the Holy Spirit who moved people to speak
